title: Service API Evolution and Observability Standards
author: Maya Chen
summary: A single, practical standard that governs API design, versioning, compatibility testing, observability instrumentation, and performance requirements for Redwood services to ensure predictable evolution and operability of inference and platform APIs.
body:
Overview:

This document establishes a combined API evolution and observability standard for Redwood services that expose programmatic interfaces to customers or internal consumers (examples: inference-proxy, model-router, telemetry-gateway). The goal is to make API changes predictable, minimize customer impact, and ensure every API is observable and measured against clear SLOs.

Goals:
- Provide clear rules for backward-compatible vs breaking changes and an approver workflow for each.
- Require contract tests and automated compatibility checks for all public and cross-team APIs.
- Standardize observable signals (traces, metrics, structured logs) and minimum retention/labeling.
- Define performance thresholds (SLOs) and testing requirements for new endpoints and major changes.

Scope:
- Applies to: REST/HTTP JSON endpoints, gRPC endpoints, and internal RPC interfaces that are relied upon across teams (e.g. model-router -> serving-runtime).
- Does NOT replace language-specific coding standards; it complements them by specifying API-level expectations.

Key Definitions:
- Public API: any endpoint documented in the public catalog or used by external customers.
- Internal API: service-to-service endpoints used within Redwood that are not customer-facing but are depended on by multiple teams.
- Contract Test: automated test verifying a consumer's expectations against a provider in CI; must be runnable in CI for each PR.

Versioning and Compatibility Rules:
1) Semantic Versioning for APIs:
   - Use a three-part version identifier in route prefixes or headers: vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH. Example: /v1.2.0/models/embedding
   - MAJOR increment = breaking changes (remove fields, change types, change semantics).
   - MINOR increment = additive, backward-compatible features (new endpoints, optional response fields).
   - PATCH increment = bug fixes and non-functional changes.

2) Stability Modes:
   - experimental: routes under /xp/ are explicitly opt-in. No stability guarantee. Feature flags and short TTLs.
   - stable: routes under /v{MAJOR} are supported per compatibility rules above.

3) Breaking Change Workflow:
   - Create an ADR (linked in the PR) describing rationale and migration plan.
   - Notify consumers: open ticket in relevant team trackers + email to api-announce for public APIs.
   - Provide a deprecation period: default 90 days for internal APIs, 180 days for public customer-facing APIs. Longer for model or data schema changes that affect state.

Contract Testing and CI Requirements:
- Every provider must ship a contract-test suite in the repository under /contracts which exposes a provider test harness.
- Consumers must include provider-based integration runs in their CI matrix (can be mocked where necessary).
- Compatibility gate: PRs that change an API must run the provider contract tests referenced by downstream consumers; if any consumer test fails, the change is blocked until addressed.
- Tooling: use the contract-runner (internal CLI) to register consumer expectations and to validate responses. Example: 

  # register a consumer contract locally
  rdx-contract register --service model-router --consumer inference-proxy --path /contracts/inference-proxy

Authentication & Authorization:
- All public and internal APIs must accept and validate short-lived service tokens (JWT or mTLS).
- For customer-facing endpoints, enforce per-token rate limits and include quota metadata in the response headers: X-Quota-Remaining, X-Quota-Reset.

Observability Requirements (per-endpoint):
Each endpoint (public or internal) must emit the following signals: 
1) Tracing: a trace span named <service>.<route> with the following tags: environment, region, customer_id (if present), model_id (if applicable), route_version. Follow our tracing semantic conventions (see /confluence/eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/tracing-conventions).
2) Metrics: counters and timers with prometheus-style names: 
   - api_requests_total{service,route,status_code} (counter)
   - api_request_duration_seconds_bucket{service,route} (histogram)
   - api_request_size_bytes_summary{service,route} (summary)
   - api_error_rate{service,route,error_type} (counter)
3) Structured Logs: JSON lines with fields: timestamp, level, service, route, request_id, trace_id, duration_ms, user_agent, client_ip (scrubbed), and a short message.

Labels and Dimensions (mandatory):
- service, route, route_version, environment, region, model_variant (if applicable), customer_tier (free/paid/enterprise), deploy_commit_sha.

Retention & Aggregation:
- Request-level logs: 14 days (hot), 180 days (cold).
- Metrics: 90 days at 1s/10s resolution, aggregated to 1m for 365 days.
- Traces: store spans for 30 days; sampling at 100% for errors and 10% for success by default.

Performance SLOs & Testing:
- Default SLOs for customer-facing inference endpoints: 
  - P50 latency <= 40ms, P95 <= 120ms, P99 <= 250ms for short-context generation endpoints (<= 256 tokens).
  - Error budget: 99.9% availability over 30d window (0.1% errors).
- For longer-sequence generation or reranking endpoints, teams must publish endpoint-specific SLOs in the service README and justify differences in the PR.
- Load testing requirements: major releases (MAJOR or MINOR) require a load test report in perf format: 
  - test harness: rdx-perf-runner v2.1 or later
  - requested load: expected 2x peak QPS for the target concurrency profile
  - metrics: p50/p95/p99, CPU/GPU utilization, queue depth, tail latency histogram

Error Classification and Alerting:
- Error classes: client_error (4xx), transient_server_error (5xx transient), permanent_server_error (5xx unrecoverable), infra_error (network/infra).
- Alerting thresholds (apply per-route): 
  - Sev2: error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m OR P95 latency > SLO * 1.5 for 5m.
  - Sev3: error rate 0.2% for 10m.
- On-call runbook: reference /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/runbooks/api-high-latency

Data Privacy and Masking:
- Requests and logs must not store full customer-inputs in plaintext. Sensitive fields must be redacted or hashed in logs. Use rdx-log-scrubber at ingestion.
- For debugging, teams may capture full payloads under gated uploads with audit logging and retention = 30 days max unless customer-authorized.

Schema Evolution for Model Payloads:
- Model input/output schemas must use explicit field names and typed envelopes. Always include an envelope version: {"schema_version": "1.0"}. Additions allowed as optional fields. Removing or renaming fields = MAJOR change.

Deprecation and Rollout Process (step-by-step):
1) Proposal: author files an ADR and a service-change ticket with owner, migration plan, and compatibility matrix.
2) Implementation: add new route/version, keep old route live, add warnings in responses: 
   - HTTP header X-Deprecation-Notice: "v1.4 retired 2025-12-31; please migrate to v2.0"
3) Canary: send 1% traffic to the new route for 48 hours while monitoring errors and latency.
4) Gradual ramp: 10% for 24h, 50% for 24h, 100% pending no regressions.
5) Cutover: after agreed deprecation window, remove old route and increment MAJOR if required.
6) Postmortem: if any failures occurred during rollout, the owning team publishes a 14-day postmortem in eng-platform/runbooks.

Tooling and Templates:
- ADR template: use /confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-template (link).
- Contract template: /tools/rdx-contract/README.md and example consumer/provider pair under examples/contracts/model-router-inference-proxy.
- Perf report template: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite/perf-report-template-2024.md

Examples and Snippets:
1) Minimal OpenAPI fragment (required metadata only):

openapi: "3.0.1"
info:
  title: Model Inference API
  version: "1.2.0"
paths:
  /v1.2.0/models/{model_id}:
    post:
      summary: Run inference
      parameters:
        - name: model_id
          in: path
          required: true
      responses:
        '200':
          description: OK

2) Example curl with tracing header and quota headers check:

curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Request-Id: $(uuidgen)" -H "X-Trace-Parent: 00-abcd1234abcd1234abcd1234abcd1234-0000000000000001-01" https://api.redwood.ai/v1.2.0/models/gpt-mini:generate -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'

Response headers must include: X-Quota-Remaining, X-Quota-Reset, X-Deprecation-Notice (if applicable).

Governance and Exceptions:
- Most changes follow the standard flow; exceptions (time-sensitive P0 fixes) require an approval from the API standards council (rotating members: eng-platform lead, runtime lead, product owner).
- Exceptions must be recorded as an ADR with the tag exception and noted in the service changelog.

Ownership and Contact List:
- API Standards Owner: Maya Chen (eng-platform).
- Contract Testing Tooling: Adrian Patel (eng-dx).
- Observability and Alerts: Sofia Martinez (eng-sre).
- Perf Benchmarks: Tom Reynolds (eng-serving-runtime).

Decision Record (summary):
- Decision: Standardize on explicit semantic-versioned route prefixes and mandatory contract tests in CI; require per-endpoint observability with set signal names and retention baselines.
- Rationale: We observed multiple customer-impacting changes in 2023–2024 due to inconsistent versioning, poor observability, and missing contract tests. Standardizing reduces breakages and shortens incident MTTR.
- Date: 2024-05-14

Appendix: Links and references:
- API design examples: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/api-examples
- Contract runner docs: /tools/rdx-contract/README.md
- Perf runner: /tools/rdx-perf-runner/CHANGELOG.md

If you are planning an API change, follow the checklist below and attach artifacts to your PR:
- [ ] ADR linked
- [ ] Contract tests added and passing
- [ ] Observability instrumentation in code + metrics dashboards created
- [ ] Perf/load test report (for major changes)
- [ ] Migration/rollback plan documented

For questions or exceptions, ping #api-standards on Slack or email api-standards@redwood.ai.
